idiom_name: type switch over the decoded message, or a map[string]handler registry filled at startup
implementation_notes: Go has neither message unions nor reflection-based dispatch, so the router is explicit: decode the envelope into a struct with a Kind field (or into per-kind structs behind an interface) and dispatch with a type switch - the construct Effective Go documents for discovering the dynamic type of an interface value - or, when the rule set should grow without touching the dispatcher, with a map[string]func(Message) error filled at startup. The map is the rules-as-data form and is what replaces the classic router object: registering a handler for a new kind is the only change a new destination needs, and the lookup miss is the fallback. Brokers remain destination-based (one consumer group per topic), so a decision that needs payload content stays in this in-process dispatcher.
pitfalls: A type switch with no matching case and no default returns silently, so an unhandled concrete type disappears without an error - make the default arm the unroutable path.
Filling the handler map at request time races with concurrent map reads (fatal error: concurrent map writes); register everything before serving or guard the registry with a sync.RWMutex.
A panic inside a worker goroutine cannot be caught by the caller and takes the process down, so validate the payload before invoking a handler (or recover at the goroutine edge).
